source.notes: A CISCE item bank of 210 competency-focused practice questions for ISC Class XI Environmental Science (not an examination paper). The cover prints 'ISC Competency Focused Practice Questions, Environmental Science, Class - XI', 'First edition: August 2026'; the preface is signed by the Chief Executive & Secretary, 31st August 2026. PDF pages 1-5 are cover, copyright, mission, preface and contents; printed page N is PDF page N+5. Questions are on PDF pages 6-68, the Answer Key on PDF pages 69-102, so answerSourceUrl equals sourceUrl. Marks come from the section headings: I MCQ (1 mark each, Q1-57), II Assertion-Reason (1 mark each, Q58-94), III Very Short Answer (1 mark each, Q95-123), IV Short Answer (2 marks each, Q124-134), V Long Answer (4 marks each, Q135-174), VI Very Long Answer (7 marks each, Q175-210); total 557. Sub-part marks printed in brackets (e.g. [2], [3]) agree with the section marks and are omitted from the text; each question is one entry. No maximum marks or duration is printed. Printed topic tags are omitted from the text and used for the chapter; cognitive tags are recorded only when all parts share one tag. Printed image/source credits (URLs, 'Source: gemini.google.com', 'AI generated' notes) are omitted from the text and flagged. The Assertion-Reason option wording varies slightly between questions and is kept as printed per question. The preface states the Answer Key 'presents the possible answers to a given question, but it is neither limiting nor exhaustive'; answers are copied verbatim (long ones trimmed with '…') and not extended. The key entries for Q126 and Q128 do not match their questions (Q128's entry repeats Q129's) and are not recorded. Some key entries look questionable and are kept for editor review (e.g. Q18 'Pastoral groups', Q19 'Global Extraction', Q51 'Indian desert and Northern plains', Q53). Some topic tags look mismatched with the question (e.g. Q104 algal blooms tagged Legal Regimes; Q91-92 tagged Design and Planning); the printed tag is followed.

questions.text:
The study of the relationships between living organisms including humans and natural systems is called Environmental Studies.
Which one of the following is the main objective of environmental studies?
options: Economic Development
Industrial Development
Human Welfare
Environmental Conservation

officialAnswer.text: (d) Environmental conservation

questions.text: “Inter-generational sensibility is reflected by a sustainable society”. The main reason to justify the above statement is the judicious use of:
options: Material resources
Natural resources
Industrial resources
Social resources

officialAnswer.text: (b) Natural resources

questions.text: Which of the following scenarios best demonstrates the multidisciplinary nature of Environmental Studies by requiring the integration of both physical/natural sciences and social sciences?
options: Analysing the chemical composition of soil to determine its nutrient content.
Engineering a new wind turbine to maximize energy output and reduce mechanical friction.
Formulating a sustainable coastal management plan that considers marine biology, oceanography, and the socioeconomic needs of local fishing communities.
Studying the population dynamics and migration patterns of a specific endangered bird species.

officialAnswer.text: (c) Formulating a sustainable coastal management plan that considers marine biology, oceanography, and the socioeconomic needs of local fishing communities.

questions.text: Which of the following disciplines is excluded from the interdisciplinary nature of Environmental Science?
options: The study of human societies and social behaviour.
The study of structure of substances and their transformation under different conditions.
The study of relationships between organisms and their environment.
The study of the positions and movement of stars and planets and the way they affect people and events.

officialAnswer.text: (d) The study of the positions and movement of stars and planets and the way they affect people and events.

questions.text: A large tech company wants to build a data centre near a wetland. The project will create many high-paying jobs for the town. However, the construction will destroy the nesting grounds of a rare bird species. Which action best reflects the human-centred viewpoint?
options: Cancelling the project entirely to protect the birds' right to exist.
Moving the data centre to a different site even if it costs the company more money.
Approving the project because the economic benefits and jobs for local families outweigh the loss of the bird population.
Pausing the project until scientists can determine how the wetland destruction will impact the global climate.

officialAnswer.text: (c) Approving the project because the economic benefits and jobs for local families outweigh the loss of the bird population.

questions.text: A State Government decides to allow a private resort to be built inside a protected forest, arguing it will create jobs for local villagers. Which Constitutional provision provides the strongest legal basis for a citizen to challenge this in court as a violation of their fundamental duty?
options: Article 48A
Article 51A(g)
73rd Constitutional Amendment
Article 21 only

officialAnswer.text: (b) Article 51A(g)

questions.text: Why is the Environment Protection Act (EPA), 1986, uniquely described as "Umbrella Legislation"?
options: It is the only law that can override the Constitution of India in environmental matters.
It provides a broad framework for the central government to coordinate activities between various authorities established under specific laws like the Water and Air Acts.
It was the first law in India to address the protection of wildlife and forests under one single document.
It prohibits any industrial activity within 10km of a water body across the entire country.

officialAnswer.text: (b) It provides a broad framework for the central government to coordinate activities between various authorities established under specific laws like the Water and Air Acts.

questions.text: In the aftermath of the Bhopal Gas Tragedy, which major shift occurred in India’s legislative approach to environmental disasters?
options: Shifting from a "Fault-based Liability" to an "Absolute Liability" regime where the enterprise is strictly responsible for hazardous leaks.
Decentralizing all industrial monitoring to the local Panchayats under the 73rd Amendment.
Making the Water Act 1974 the primary law for controlling toxic gas emissions.
Abolishing the need for Environmental Impact Assessments for large chemical plants.

officialAnswer.text: (a) Shifting from a "Fault-based Liability" to an "Absolute Liability" regime where the enterprise is strictly responsible for hazardous leaks.

questions.text: Under the Forest (Conservation) Act 1980, if a state wants to "de-reserve" a portion of a reserved forest for a non-forest purpose, whose prior permission is mandatory?
options: The local Gram Sabha under the 73rd Amendment
The State Governor
The Central Government
The National Green Tribunal

officialAnswer.text: (c) The Central Government.

questions.text: A researcher discovers a unique medicinal plant in a remote village and wants to export its seeds for commercial drug development in Europe. Under the Biological Diversity Act 2002, what is the primary requirement?
options: Obtaining a permit from the Wildlife Warden under the Wildlife Protection Act.
Approval from the National Biodiversity Authority (NBA) to ensure equitable benefit sharing.
Notifying the local municipality under the 74th Amendment only.
No permission is needed if the researcher is an Indian citizen.

officialAnswer.text: (b) Approval from the National Biodiversity Authority (NBA) to ensure equitable benefit sharing.

questions.text: The 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendment Acts support environmental protection primarily by:
options: Giving the Supreme Court the power to appoint local mayors.
Empowering Panchayats and Municipalities to prepare plans for economic development and social justice, including environmental protection and conservation.
Transferring the power of the NGT to local village courts.
Making the "Polluter Pays Principle" a mandatory part of village bylaws only.

officialAnswer.text: (b) Empowering Panchayats and Municipalities to prepare plans for economic development and social justice, including environmental protection and conservation.

questions.text: How does the Wildlife Protection Act 1972 balance human-animal conflict regarding "vermin" animals?
options: It allows citizens to hunt any animal that enters their farmland without a permit.
It empowers the Central Government to declare certain wild animals as "vermin" for a specific area and period, removing them from protection schedules temporarily.
It mandates that all wild animals be relocated to zoos if they cross forest boundaries.
It provides absolute protection to all species, prohibiting any form of culling regardless of the threat to crops.

officialAnswer.text: (b) It empowers the Central Government to declare certain wild animals as "vermin" for a specific area and period, removing them from protection schedules temporarily.

questions.text: If an industry is found discharging untreated chemical effluents into a stream, which specific power granted by the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act 1974 is most likely to be used for immediate closure?
options: Power to arrest the CEO without a warrant.
Power to give directions to cut off electricity or water supply to the defaulting unit.
Power to seize the land and gift it to the 73rd Amendment local bodies.
Power to file a lawsuit in a civil court which takes 10 years to resolve.

officialAnswer.text: (b) Power to give directions to cut off electricity or water supply to the defaulting unit.

questions.text: Under the Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act 1981, "noise" was included as an air pollutant through an amendment. What does this imply for enforcement?
options: Noise is only a pollutant if it occurs near a water body.
State Pollution Control Boards have the authority to regulate ambient noise levels from industrial and commercial sources.
Only the police, and not the Pollution Boards, can monitor noise.
Noise pollution is only applicable to vehicles and not factories.

officialAnswer.text: (b) State Pollution Control Boards have the authority to regulate ambient noise levels from industrial and commercial sources.

questions.text: The National Environmental Policy (NEP) 2006 emphasises the "Precautionary Principle." This means:
options: Action to protect the environment should only be taken when there is 100% scientific certainty of damage.
Where there are threats of serious or irreversible damage, lack of full scientific certainty shall not be used as a reason for postponing cost-effective measures to prevent degradation.
The government must wait for a disaster to happen before passing a law.
Development must always take precedence over environmental concerns.

officialAnswer.text: (b) Where there are threats of serious or irreversible damage, lack of full scientific certainty shall not be used as a reason for postponing cost-effective measures to prevent degradation.

questions.text: Under the Waste Management Rules (updated in 2022), the concept of "Extended Producer Responsibility" (EPR) shifts the burden of waste management:
options: Entirely onto the consumer who buys the product.
To the local municipality to find land for landfills.
To the producers/manufacturers to ensure the environmentally sound management of their products until the end of their life cycle.
To the NGT to collect waste from households.

officialAnswer.text: (c) To the producers/manufacturers to ensure the environmentally sound management of their products until the end of their life cycle.

questions.text: Why was the National Green Tribunal (NGT) established as a "specialized" body
options: To handle only criminal cases related to wildlife poaching.
To provide a forum for speedy environmental justice and handle cases involving multi-disciplinary issues (law and ecology) through judicial and expert members.
To replace the Supreme Court of India in all civil matters.
To act as a subsidiary of the Ministry of Environment and Forests.

officialAnswer.text: (b) To provide a forum for speedy environmental justice and handle cases involving multi-disciplinary issues (law and ecology) through judicial and expert members.

questions.text: Article 48A and Article 51A(g) differ primarily in that:
options: 48A is a duty of the State to protect the environment, while 51A(g) is a fundamental duty of the individual citizen.
48A is enforceable in a court of law, while 51A(g) is not.
48A applies only to forests, while 51A(g) applies only to wildlife.
There is no difference; they are identical in wording and intent.

officialAnswer.text: (a) 48A is a duty of the State to protect the environment, while 51A(g) is a fundamental duty of the individual citizen.

questions.text: A state government proposes a high-speed highway through a notified Wildlife Sanctuary. However, a conservation group moves the National Green Tribunal (NGT). Based on the National Environmental Policy (2006) and the Wildlife Protection Act 1972, which principle would the NGT most likely apply to halt the project?
options: Precautionary Principle: Since the highway poses a risk of irreversible damage to biodiversity, the lack of scientific certainty regarding the exact loss shouldn't prevent protective measures.

officialAnswer.text: (a) Precautionary Principle: Since the highway poses a risk of irreversible damage to biodiversity, the lack of scientific certainty regarding the exact loss shouldn't prevent protective measures.

officialAnswer.text: • A landscape is never static because ecosystems undergo ecological succession. Biotic (living) and abiotic (non-living) factors continuously interact, alter, and modify the environment over time. • Ecosystems constantly try to achieve a state of equilibrium or climax community (stable balance). However, this balance is dynamic, not permanent, because the environment keeps changing. • Natural Disturbances: Events like floods, earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, or forest fires disrupt existing habitats. This forces the ecosystem to restart succession to regain balance. • Human (Anthropogenic) Activities: Deforestation, industrialisation, and urbanization constantly alter landscapes. These actions fragment habitats and force species to adapt or perish, disrupting the food web. • Climate Change and Shifting Resources: Gradual changes in temperature, rainfall, and resource availability alter the carrying capacity of the environment, forcing species to compete or migrate. • Biotic Interactions: The introduction of invasive alien species or sudden population explosions of pests creates a biological challenge, forcing the ecosystem to restructure its food chains.
